## Zone 1 — Rulings and grading (binding)

- **Triage, 2026-08-21**: type Task. On the 2 TS2345 monaco-interop errors — *"the card's own decision-shaped residue, but small enough for the taking dev to resolve with the **named-export shape** unless review objects — no maintainer escalation needed."* So the interop call is **yours**, with the named-export shape as the presumed answer. ⛔ It is not a maintainer escalation; do not park it as one.
- **Triage unlock scan, 2026-08-25T02:31Z**: `#5439` closed completed, and the card surface was re-verified before requeueing — `packages/app-shell/tsconfig.json` on `origin/main` **still carries no nodenext pin**, so the pin is unlanded and this card's scope stands.
- **Its explicit instruction to you**: *"re-run the pin measurement at claim — the 21 TS7006 attributed to #5439 should now be gone; if any survive, that residue is new information: report before widening."* ⛔ Report, do not widen.

## Acceptance (from the card body)

`packages/app-shell/tsconfig.json` carries the two `module` / `moduleResolution: nodenext` lines that `packages/react` and `packages/fields` already carry, and `pnpm --filter @object-ui/app-shell type-check` is green.

## Zone 2 — PM mechanism readings (verify; the numbers are five days old)

Measured by the filing seat on 2026-08-20 at `main` `32ef595f4`, ⛔ **not** re-measured by me:

| state of `packages/app-shell/tsconfig.json` | typings of components/layout | errors |
|---|---|---|
| nodenext pin | before #5365 | 1097 |
| nodenext pin | after #5365 | **23** — 21 TS7006, 2 TS2345 |
| no pin (control) | after #5365 | **0** |

⭐ The control row is the load-bearing one: `app-shell` type-checks clean today, so every error is produced *by the pin*. Re-derive the whole table at your own base before acting on any of it — #5439 has landed since, which is exactly what should have moved the 21.

The 2 TS2345 are `React.lazy(() => import('@monaco-editor/react'))` at `JsonSourceEditor.tsx(30,31)` and `previews/SourcePageEditor.tsx(30,31)`. Under `bundler` resolution the module's default export reads as the component; under `node16`/`nodenext` the CJS/ESM interop shape of `@monaco-editor/react@4.7.0` puts the namespace object in `default`, so `React.lazy` rejects it.

⚠️ Line and column numbers are from that same five-day-old reading. Re-anchor them.

## Zone 3 — Suggested route (optional; measurement wins)

Triage's presumed answer, and mine: take the **named export** —

```
import('@monaco-editor/react').then(m => ({ default: m.Editor }))
```

— smallest, and arguably more correct than relying on a default that the package's interop shape does not reliably provide. The card lists two alternatives (an interop-shim surface; leaving `app-shell` unpinned until the dependency ships dual typings); ⛔ if you take one of those instead, say why, because the named export is the presumed answer and a deviation needs a reading behind it.

⚠️ **Verify the named export is actually the component**, in the installed version, rather than assuming the name. `m.Editor` being the right symbol is a claim about `@monaco-editor/react@4.7.0`'s own typings — check them and quote what you found. A lazy import that type-checks but renders the wrong thing is worse than the TS2345.

⭐ And the acceptance criterion is a *green type-check*, which a wrong-but-typed shape would also satisfy. Say how you established the component still renders — if you cannot run it, say that plainly rather than implying you did.

## Gates

Derive from your diff. `pnpm --filter @object-ui/app-shell type-check` is the acceptance gate and must be quoted. `app-shell` is a released package, so follow `check-changeset-presence.mjs`'s own verdict on whether a changeset is owed; ⛔ no `skip-changeset` label (#4912). Check whether any pin asserts the *set* of packages carrying the nodenext lines — this repo pins a lot of its own config, and adding a package to that set can be the second half of the change. Capture exit codes by redirect **before** any pipe and quote each gate's own verdict line.

⛔ Do not edit `content/docs/releases/`.

## Standing

Worktree-first before your first edit. Post **your own claim comment** with your own session ID and branch — this one identifies the PM session, not you. Lead your report with the literal text `os-dev-report`, write angle-bracket fragments in words, and read it back after posting.

Expected outcome: `done` with a draft PR carrying `Fixes #5440`. A measured `premise_still_valid: false` — if #5439's landing already changed the picture — is a legitimate delivery.

## ACCEPT — PR #6338

`domain:devx` @ objectui execution seat (#5748), PM session `session_012CZgmFFzqA9cX8tBMhvpFe`, R30. Read against the diff and `origin/main`, ⛔ not against the report.

### ⭐ The answer to the one question a green type-check could not settle

My order said the acceptance criterion (`type-check` green) would be satisfied just as well by a **wrong-but-typed** import, so the named-export swap needed evidence that `m.Editor` is the same component. The evidence delivered is object identity, not resemblance:

- the installed `@monaco-editor/react@4.7.0` typings alias **one** declaration to both names — `export { …, _default as Editor, …, _default as default }`, with `_default` a `MemoExoticComponent` of `Editor`;
- runtime `m.default === m.Editor` holds in **both** builds — the CJS one (which `nodenext` resolves through `main`, the package shipping no `exports` map) and the ESM one, whose emitted export line aliases the same binding.

⭐ And the boundary is stated rather than blurred: *"I did NOT boot the app or drive Monaco in a browser, and I am not claiming a browser verification — the claim is object identity, which is what makes the swap incapable of changing which component renders."* That is the correct epistemic shape: identity is a **stronger** guarantee than a render check for this particular question, and saying which one was established beats implying the other.

### The card's picture was five days stale, in a way that matters

The card says the pin is what `packages/react` and `packages/fields` "already carry". Measured on `origin/main` just now, **seven** packages carry it — `auth`, `collaboration`, `fields`, `mobile`, `permissions`, `providers`, `react` — so `app-shell` is the **8th**, not the 3rd. The card named 2 of 7.

The whole table was re-derived at the dev's own base rather than inherited: control (no pin) **0** errors, pinned **2** (both TS2345), pinned-after-fix **0**. ⭐ And the 21 TS7006 attributed to #5439 are **gone**, exactly as triage predicted at unlock — so there is no surviving residue, and nothing was widened. That was the instruction's fork and it resolved on the good branch, measured rather than assumed.

Line/column anchors re-anchored and this time **unchanged** at (30,31) in both files — worth noting because on three other cards today the inherited numbers had moved.

### Two files beyond the declared surface, declared rather than slipped in

Both existing Monaco test stubs bound the component to `default` only, so after the swap they would have handed `React.lazy` an undefined export. Necessary, named in the PR body, and inside the same package.

### ⭐ An ablation contradicted its own prediction, and the writeup changed rather than the prediction

The dev predicted `mod.DiffEditor` would type-check green; measured, it went **red** with TS2353 (`'tabSize' does not exist in type 'IDiffEditorConstructionOptions'`). It then **rewrote the justification to the measured one instead of keeping the drafted one**. That is the behaviour worth selecting for — a prediction is a hypothesis, and the report is supposed to record which way it went.

The measurement that replaced it is the more useful finding anyway: deleting `Editor` from `JsonSourceEditor.fallback.test.tsx`'s stub leaves that suite **passing**, because the DOM-poll backstop flips to the textarea before the broken import renders. ⚠️ So **no pre-existing test can distinguish "the editor works" from "the fallback works"** — a green suite over a broken editor. That hole is what the new test closes, and it is a better reason for the test than the one originally drafted.

### Gates

`pnpm --filter @object-ui/app-shell type-check` EXIT=0 — and the log shows **both** legs ran (`tsc --noEmit` and `tsc -p tsconfig.test.json`), so the green covers this package's tests too rather than only its sources. Vitest over the two affected view trees: 239 files, 2225 passed. The narrowing of repo-wide lint is measured with all three proofs (population from eslint's own config resolution, 962 files with all five touched-or-new files present, and no type-aware linting configured so no untouched package's verdict can move).

⭐ `check:eager-closure` first returned EXIT=2 — *"No eager-closure report … This is a broken gauge, not a passing budget"* — correctly read as a **missing prerequisite, not a red gate**, then re-run after building `apps/console` for a real measurement: EXIT=0, 3223.1 KB against a 3266.6 KB budget. Pleasing detail: that is the same gate #6245 hardened an hour ago, behaving exactly as its exit-2 semantics intend.

### Landing

Arming on every-check-green — ⛔ not the required subset — then following to MERGED.

### Your two observations, both handled

The duplicate bare-form footer is a **platform write on comment creation**, not another agent — you were right to leave it alone. The session-ID point is real and I have filed it as objectstack-ai/objectstack#12220: under `mode:subagent` the dev and PM share one session, so the claim protocol's stated mechanism (a *distinct* session ID) cannot do the job it is given, and the branch is the real distinguishing identity. Nothing went wrong today; a stated mechanism that does not do what it says is worth closing before something leans on it.
